### Observed differences

- The three activities **A36, A37 and A42** ran in every trace in the earlier window (200 of 200); in the later window they run together in only about 47 in 100 traces (94–96 of 200), and in about 52 in 100 later traces none of them appears. They still appear only as a group, and their internal order remains unfixed in both windows. [OCC032, OCC033, OCC037, REL025, REL026, REL027]
- **A27** also dropped from every trace to about 54 in 100 (107 of 200), and it has become mutually exclusive with that group: A27 co-occurred with A36/A37/A42 in all earlier traces but in only about 0–1 in 100 later traces. [OCC025, REL016, REL017, REL018]
- The group moved later in the trace: its mean relative position went from about 0.40 to about 0.57–0.58, while A26 moved earlier (about 0.60 to 0.54), A28 earlier (about 0.45 to 0.39) and A27 slightly earlier within the traces containing it (about 0.62 to 0.58). [POS006, POS007, POS008, POS002, POS004, POS003]
- After **A25**, the group disappeared from its old spot: earlier, about 99 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions led to A42, A36 or A37 (roughly 34/33/31 per 100) and A28 followed about four steps later (94 in 100); in the later window A25 leads directly to A28 in about 98–99 in 100 cases, at a distance of one step in about 98 in 100. [DIR025, LAG001]
- After **A26**, the routing split: earlier A26 led to A27 in about 97–98 in 100 cases and A27 led to A31 in about 98–99 in 100, with the group always earlier in the trace; in the later window A26 leads to A27 in about 52 in 100 cases and to one of A36/A37/A42 in about 46–47 in 100, with the group then preceding A31. The A26→A31 distance was two steps in about 97 in 100 earlier traces; later it is two steps in about 51 in 100 (via A27) and four steps in about 46 in 100 (via the three-activity group). [DIR026, DIR027, REL011, REL022, LAG006]
- Outside this cluster, several activities shifted participation by about 5–9 percentage points (A01, A05, A07, A10 and A21 down; A03, A11, A12, A13, A48 and A49 up), with small matching shifts in a few routing shares. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC005, OCC007, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, OCC020, OCC042, OCC043, DIR003, DIR007, DIR011, DIR013]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural rerouting of the segment formed by **A36, A37 and A42**. In the earlier window, every trace ran A25, then these three activities in unfixed order, then A28, and later A26 → A27 → A31. In the later window, A25 passes directly to A28, and the three-activity group reappears in only about 47 in 100 traces, inserted between A26 and A31, where it acts as an alternative to A27: a trace now either takes A26 → A27 → A31 (about 52 in 100) or A26 → the group → A31 (about 46–47 in 100), with A27 and the group almost never co-occurring. This is supported directly by successor changes (A25 from the group to A28 in ~98–99 in 100; A26 split ~52/47 between A27 and the group), order relations (A26 now precedes the group, which now precedes A31), distances (A25→A28 from four steps in 94 in 100 to one step in ~98 in 100; A26→A31 split ~51/46 between two and four steps), position shifts (group mean position ~0.40 → ~0.57–0.58), and participation drops from 200 of 200 traces to about 94–96 — far beyond what sampling between two 200-trace windows produces for activities this frequent, and consistent across the occurrence, position, direction, relation and lag indicators. Limitations: positions are event orders rather than clock times, so "moved later" refers to sequence position; the evidence cannot rule out that the later routing already existed as a variant too rare to appear in the earlier 200-trace window; and no chance-expectation baseline was provided with this evidence, so the screening comparison rests on the size of these participation changes. [OCC025, OCC032, OCC033, OCC037, DIR025, DIR026, LAG001, LAG006, POS006, REL011, REL016, REL022]

Other differences: several activities outside this cluster shifted participation by about 5–9 percentage points (A01, A05, A07, A10, A21 down; A03, A11, A12, A13, A48, A49 up) with small routing shifts among early activities; these are not explained by the rerouting above and may reflect sampling variation between the two windows. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC005, OCC007, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, OCC020, OCC042, OCC043, DIR003, DIR007, DIR011, DIR013]
